facts.fact: The document states that the national ICT development policy PNDTIC (2010-2025) was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 13 July 2011.
The policy's title and vision set its period as 2010-2025, with a vision to 2025 of universal ICT access and regional centre of excellence status.

The policy text is hosted as a PDF on the Primature's official site (primature.gov.bi, uploaded 2026/06 per the URL); the document itself gives no publication date, so the document's published date of 2011-07-13 applies to its adoption only.

facts.fact: CIPESA reports that the Cabinet, meeting on 13 July 2011, adopted the 2010-2025 National ICT Development Plan (PNDTIC) to accelerate economic growth and promote universal ICT access.
CIPESA describes the National ICT Development Plan adopted in 2011 as a 15-year plan covering 2010-2025.

CIPESA states that implementation of the 2010-2025 National ICT Development Plan is well underway, citing 1,250 km of fibre laid by the Burundi Backbone System, and measures it against no target in the plan; the report gives no event date, so its publication date of January 2020 is used.
CIPESA states that in 2007 the government passed the National ICT policy to spur economic development through ICT.

facts.fact: ABP reports that public-sector ICT focal points met from 31 May to 2 June 2021 to review progress in applying the national ICT development policy PNDTIC 2010-2025, treating it as the policy in force.
The report names the policy as PNDTIC 2010-2025 and says it is to be implemented effectively by 2025, with universal ICT access as the 2025 vision.

The focal points' retreat found achievements in infrastructure, applications, skills, planning and governance but gives no figures against the policy's targets, and says more effort is needed by 2025.
The retreat stressed the ministry in charge of ICT as key to coordinating the stakeholders and to monitoring and evaluating the PNDTIC, and asked that ICT cells be set up in all institutions.
